confusions: The Who pays page gives the top 1% share of Income Tax, the share of income, and a 46.0% figure for the richest fifth, and I could not tell which of these numbers answered which question.
The G7 tax and spending chart has a Taxes and Spending switch, and I nearly read the spending ranking from the tax chart.
The 36.2% and 46.0% numbers on the Who pays page look like the same kind of share, and I was not sure which one was a share of income.
I could not find anything on the site about the top 1% share of all taxes, so I could not tell whether the site says it leaves that out.
The Year by year page is about everyday life and does not show years of data, so I did not find the figures I was looking for there.
The immigration page has very long quoted paragraphs in small print, and I stopped reading them before the end.
Defence has two figures for the same year, 2.1 percent of GDP on the spending page and 2.32 percent on the NATO part, and I was not sure which to use.
I could not find any OECD structural reform figures on the site, and the Sources page only lists a few OECD datasets, so the reform questions were left as not sure.
The productivity chart's Since 2008 switch and its ranking table were hard to tell apart, and I had to look at both.
On the manifesto pages, the Back button jumped to the Questions page instead of the pledge list, so I had to walk back to the list several times.
Pledge pages were long, and the answer was not always in the first line, so I had to scroll a long way for each one.
The Why is UK government debt high page is very long with many quotes, so I gave up before the end of the page.
The housing and welfare pages are long, and I could not find the welfare, tuition fee or 1999 house price figures before my actions ran low.
The housing compare tool shows the table far down the page with no clear heading, so I could not find the England owner-occupier figures.
